correctness.rationale: The theorem is for the exact Bagchi–Datta labeled CP2_10. Independently reconstructed all 48 five-vertex facets from five published A4 orbits (group order 12), face counts (10,45,110,120,48), all 35 missing tetrahedra among 210 four-subsets, the diagonal {x11,x22,x33,x44}, and full A4 orbit lengths 1,4,6,12,12. Independently assembled integral oriented boundary matrices and evaluated the provided 36×36 ∂2 determinant +1 and 73×73 ∂3 determinant −1 from the actual checker indices. Rank(∂1)=9, ∂2∂3=0 and cocycle upper bound yield rank(∂2)=36, rank(∂3)=73. The explicitly inspected integral 2-cocycle annihilates all 120 tetrahedral boundaries; independently re-evaluated its values on every 35 missing-tetrahedron boundary: 34 absolute values 1 and one 2, on the diagonal. The unit minor makes im∂3 primitive; H2≈Z and a value-one cycle is primitive. A nonzero 2-cycle on four vertices necessarily is the oriented full tetrahedron boundary, and fewer than four vertices cannot support one. This is an exhaustive exact finite certificate; it does not classify larger support or other triangulations.
residual_risks: Published combinatorial census or precomputed Smith tables might duplicate this finite result under a different vertex labeling.
